cases.description: Both entry and exit are null → position is not opened.
Entry trade is set, exit is still null → position is opened.
Entry is null but exit is non‑null (illegal state) → position is not opened.
Both entry and exit are non‑null (position already closed) → position is not opened.
A newly created Position is opened by calling `operate(index)` which creates the entry trade (exit remains null). After this operation `isOpened()` must return true.
A Position that has been opened (entry set) and then closed by calling `operate(index)` a second time (which creates the exit trade) must report `isOpened()` as false.

A Position that was opened, then its entry trade is manually cleared (e.g., via reflection or a setter) while the exit trade remains null. Even though the exit is still null, the absence of an entry means the position is not opened, so `isOpened()` returns false.
